title: Job Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Job chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Job Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Job Chapter 15.

questions.question: Who answered Eliphaz the Temanite in Job 15?
questions.explanation: Eliphaz the Temanite is the one who spoke in Job 15:1.

questions.question: True or False: Eliphaz suggests that wise men should not speak vain knowledge.
questions.explanation: In Job 15:2, Eliphaz questions whether a wise man should utter vain knowledge.

questions.question: What does Eliphaz accuse Job of casting off?
questions.explanation: Eliphaz states that Job has cast off fear in Job 15:4.

questions.question: True or False: According to Eliphaz, Job's mouth does not condemn him.
questions.explanation: Eliphaz claims in Job 15:6 that Job's own mouth condemns him.

questions.question: What does Eliphaz ask Job regarding the first man?
options: Are you the first man that was born?
Were you made before the hills?
Have you seen the face of God?
Do you know the beginning of time?
questions.correctAnswer: Are you the first man that was born?
questions.explanation: Eliphaz questions Job if he is the first man born in Job 15:7.

questions.question: True or False: Eliphaz believes Job has heard the secret of God.
questions.explanation: Eliphaz questions in Job 15:8 if Job has heard the secret of God, implying he has not.

questions.question: According to Eliphaz, who is older than Job's father?
questions.explanation: Eliphaz states in Job 15:10 that there are grayheaded and aged men much older than Job's father.

questions.question: What does Eliphaz imply about the consolations of God?
questions.explanation: In Job 15:11, Eliphaz asks if the consolations of God are small with Job.

questions.question: True or False: Eliphaz questions why Job's heart carries him away.
questions.explanation: Eliphaz does question why Job's heart carries him away in Job 15:12.

questions.question: In Job 15, what does Eliphaz suggest Job's words have done?
questions.explanation: Eliphaz states in Job 15:13 that Job's words have turned his spirit against God.

questions.question: According to Eliphaz, what is man in terms of cleanliness?
questions.explanation: Eliphaz states in Job 15:16 that man is abominable and filthy.

medium.title: Job Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Job Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Job 15:14 suggest about the nature of man?
options: Man is born of a woman
Man is not clean or righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Man is not clean or righteous
questions.explanation: Job 15:14 asks, 'What is man, that he should be clean? and he which is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?' This implies that man is not clean or inherently righteous.

questions.question: According to Job 15:16, how does the chapter describe the wicked man?
questions.explanation: Job 15:16 states, 'How much more abominable and filthy is man, which drinketh iniquity like water?' indicating the wicked man's state.

questions.question: Job 15:20 mentions the condition of the wicked man. What does it say about his experience?
options: He travails with pain all his days
questions.correctAnswer: He travails with pain all his days
questions.explanation: Job 15:20 states, 'The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days,' reflecting the suffering that accompanies wickedness.

questions.question: What does Job 15:21 indicate about the mindset of the wicked man during prosperity?
questions.explanation: Job 15:21 says, 'A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him,' showing his anxiety even in good times.

questions.question: What does Job 15:23 reveal about the wicked man's search for sustenance?
questions.explanation: Job 15:23 states, 'He wandereth abroad for bread, saying, Where is it?' indicating the desperation of the wicked in seeking sustenance.

questions.question: According to Job 15:24, what emotions will trouble and anguish bring upon the wicked?
questions.explanation: Job 15:24 says, 'Trouble and anguish shall make him afraid; they shall prevail against him,' indicating the overwhelming fear that troubles bring.

questions.question: How does Job 15:30 describe the fate of the wicked man's substance?
options: It shall be shared with the needy
questions.explanation: Job 15:29 states, 'He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue,' showing the fleeting nature of the wicked's wealth.

questions.question: What does Job 15:32 say about the timing of the wicked's fate?
options: It will happen in due time
It shall be accomplished before his time
It will happen after his death
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be accomplished before his time
questions.explanation: Job 15:32 states, 'It shall be accomplished before his time,' indicating that the wicked will face judgment unexpectedly.

questions.question: Based on Job 15:35, what is the outcome for the congregation of hypocrites?
questions.explanation: Job 15:34 states, 'For the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate,' indicating the inevitable downfall of those who are hypocritical.

questions.question: True or False: According to Job 15:15, God puts trust in His saints.
questions.explanation: Job 15:15 states, 'Behold, he putteth no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight,' indicating that even the saints are not fully trusted.

questions.question: True or False: Job 15:17 suggests that Eliphaz is willing to share wisdom that has been revealed to him.
questions.explanation: Job 15:17 says, 'I will shew thee, hear me; and that which I have seen I will declare,' indicating Eliphaz's willingness to share his insights.

questions.question: True or False: Job 15:22 states that the wicked man believes he will come out of darkness.
questions.explanation: Job 15:22 states, 'He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness,' indicating his despair and lack of hope.

hard.title: Job Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Job Chapter 15.

questions.question: What does Eliphaz accuse Job of doing with his mouth?
questions.explanation: Eliphaz states, 'For thy mouth uttereth thine iniquity' (Job 15:5), indicating that he believes Job's words are filled with wrongdoing.

questions.question: According to Job 15, what is said about the wicked man's condition?
questions.explanation: Job 15:20 states, 'The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days,' emphasizing the continual suffering of the wicked.

questions.question: What does Eliphaz suggest about man's ability to be clean?
questions.explanation: Eliphaz rhetorically asks, 'What is man, that he should be clean?' (Job 15:14), suggesting that it is impossible for man to achieve cleanliness or righteousness.

questions.question: How does Job 15 describe the fate of the wicked?
questions.explanation: Job 15:22 mentions that 'He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword,' indicating a grim fate for the wicked.

questions.question: Which literary device is exemplified by the phrase 'he shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue'?
questions.explanation: The phrase demonstrates parallelism, where both parts of the statement express similar ideas about the fate of the wicked (Job 15:29).

questions.question: What does Job 15 say about the congregation of hypocrites?
questions.explanation: In Job 15:34, it is stated, 'For the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate,' indicating their eventual downfall.

questions.question: True or False: Eliphaz believes that Job is speaking wise and profitable words.
questions.explanation: Eliphaz questions whether a wise man should 'utter vain knowledge' (Job 15:2), implying that he does not view Job's words as wise or profitable.

questions.question: According to Job 15, what do the wicked drink iniquity like?
questions.explanation: Job 15:16 states, 'How much more abominable and filthy is man, which drinketh iniquity like water?', illustrating the pervasive nature of wickedness.

questions.question: What is implied about Job in relation to the wisdom of the aged men mentioned?
options: He does not listen to them
questions.explanation: Eliphaz contrasts Job's views with those of 'the grayheaded and very aged men' (Job 15:10), implying Job lacks their wisdom.

questions.question: What does Job 15 suggest about trusting in vanity?
options: It is a sign of faith
questions.explanation: Job 15:31 warns, 'Let not him that is deceived trust in vanity: for vanity shall be his recompence,' indicating that such trust leads to negative outcomes.

questions.question: True or False: Job is accused of restraining prayer before God.
questions.explanation: Eliphaz asserts, 'Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God' (Job 15:4), clearly accusing Job of not praying.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of the wicked facing judgment for their deeds?
questions.explanation: Psalm 1 discusses the fate of the wicked, similar to Job 15's depiction of their suffering and judgment, particularly in verses about their downfall.

questions.question: What does the word 'vanity' in Job 15:31 imply in its original Hebrew context?
questions.explanation: 'Vanity' in the original Hebrew indicates something that is fleeting or without substance, leading to a warning against trusting in it (Job 15:31).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to the theme of hypocrisy and judgment found in Job 15?
questions.explanation: Matthew 7 addresses the theme of hypocrisy and warns against judging others while being hypocritical, resonating with Job 15's critique of the wicked.

theological.title: Job Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Job Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Job 15:2 suggest about the nature of wisdom?
options: It is filled with vain knowledge
questions.correctAnswer: It is filled with vain knowledge
questions.explanation: Job 15:2 indicates that a wise man should not utter vain knowledge, implying that true wisdom is not characterized by triviality or emptiness.

questions.question: According to Job 15:14, what is said about the nature of man?
questions.explanation: Job 15:14 emphasizes the fallen nature of humanity, asserting that no one born of a woman can be righteous, reflecting human sinfulness.

questions.question: What does Job 15:20 reveal about the experience of the wicked?
questions.explanation: Job 15:20 states that the wicked man travails with pain all his days, highlighting the suffering that accompanies a life of wickedness.

questions.question: According to Job 15:27, what physical state is described of the wicked?
options: They cover their face with fatness
questions.correctAnswer: They cover their face with fatness
questions.explanation: Job 15:27 describes the wicked as covering their face with fatness, symbolizing a false sense of security and indulgence in sin.

questions.question: What does Job 15:31 suggest about the nature of trust in vanity?
options: It is a source of hope
questions.explanation: Job 15:31 warns that trusting in vanity will lead to deception, emphasizing the futility of relying on empty pursuits.

questions.question: How does Job 15:11 inquire about the nature of God's consolations?
questions.explanation: Job 15:11 questions whether the consolations of God are small, suggesting that the comfort offered by God should not be taken lightly.

questions.question: What does Job 15:35 say about the outcome of the wicked's actions?
questions.explanation: Job 15:35 points out that the wicked conceive mischief and bring forth vanity, illustrating the destructive fruit of their actions.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 5-6 and verse 14 convey about human speech?
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 indicate that one's own mouth can condemn them, while verse 14 highlights the unclean nature of man, suggesting that speech is a reflection of one's inner condition.

questions.question: What does Job 15:10 imply about the wisdom of the aged?
options: It is greater than Job's father's
questions.correctAnswer: It is greater than Job's father's
questions.explanation: Job 15:10 states that there are wise men much elder than Job's father, implying that the wisdom of the aged is to be respected and acknowledged.

questions.question: According to Job 15:19, who was the earth given to?
questions.explanation: Job 15:19 mentions that the earth was given to a particular group, emphasizing the exclusivity of their inheritance and the special relationship they have with God.

questions.question: What does Job 15:22 reveal about the mindset of the wicked?
options: They are hopeful for the future
They believe in their return from darkness
questions.explanation: Job 15:22 indicates that the wicked believe they will not return from darkness, reflecting a mindset filled with despair and fear of judgment.

questions.question: How does Job 15:29 portray the fate of the wicked?
options: They will not prolong their perfection
questions.correctAnswer: They will not prolong their perfection
questions.explanation: Job 15:29 states that the wicked will not be rich or prolong their perfection, indicating their ultimate downfall and lack of lasting success.

questions.question: What specific attribute of God is revealed in Job 15:15 regarding His view of creation?
questions.explanation: Job 15:15 indicates that God does not trust in His saints and sees the heavens as unclean, demonstrating His justice in judging all creation.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be gained from Job 15:24 about the struggles of the wicked?
questions.explanation: Job 15:24 describes the wicked as being filled with trouble and anguish, highlighting the consequences of their sinful choices.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not punish sin. What does Job 15:25-26 teach?
questions.explanation: Job 15:25-26 depicts the wicked as stretching out their hand against God, suggesting that divine retribution is imminent for those who oppose Him.
